annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Porter" on page 561 within "The Bedroom Scene": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "Porter" on page 561 ("The Bedroom Scene"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
